translationRepairs: s0032 Chinese is （午）; the idiomatic (chen) wrongly copies the following unit’s 辰, and (wu) matches this unit’s gloss.
Xiao Tanzhi, protector-general of the army, was sent at the head of the six armies to crush the rebellion.
Xiao Tanzhi, Leader of the Army, was sent at the head of the six armies to crush the rebellion.
s0035 has 領軍將軍, a distinct office from 護軍將軍; rendering it as protector-general conflates the two, and Leader of the Army restores the correct title.
Protector-General of the Army Xiao Tanzhi was dispatched to lead the six armies to attack him.
Leader of the Army Xiao Tanzhi was dispatched to lead the six armies to attack him.
The literal of s0035 likewise turns 領軍將軍 into Protector-General of the Army; Leader of the Army corrects that office without other changes.
Day jisi: Xu Xiaosi, director of the masters of writing, became minister of works; Liu Xuan, right guards general, became protector-general of the army.
Day jisi: Xu Xiaosi, director of the masters of writing, became minister of works; Liu Xuan, right guards general, became Leader of the Army.
s0038’s 為領軍將軍 again makes Liu Xuan Leader of the Army, not protector-general (護軍); the proposed idiomatic fixes that office error.
Day jisi: Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi was made Minister of Works; Right Guards General Liu Xuan was made Protector-General of the Army.
Day jisi: Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi was made Minister of Works; Right Guards General Liu Xuan was made Leader of the Army.
The literal repeats the same 領軍/護軍 conflation for Liu Xuan’s appointment; Leader of the Army matches 領軍將軍.
Day xinwei: Wang Ying, crown prince household head, became central protector-general of the army.
Day xinwei: Wang Ying, crown prince household head, became Central Leader of the Army.
s0043 has 中領軍, in the 領軍 series, not a 護軍/protector-general title; Central Leader of the Army is the accurate office name.
Day xinwei: Crown Prince Household Head Wang Ying was made Central Protector-General of the Army.
Day xinwei: Crown Prince Household Head Wang Ying was made Central Leader of the Army.
The literal likewise misrenders 中領軍 as Central Protector-General; Central Leader of the Army corrects it.

Winter, tenth month, day yiwei: Xu Xiaosi, director of the masters of writing and newly made minister of works, was put to death, as was Shen Wenji, right vice director and newly made army-pacifying general.

Winter, tenth month, day yiwei: Xu Xiaosi, director of the masters of writing and newly made minister of works, was put to death, as was Shen Wenji, right vice director and newly made garrison general.
s0044’s 鎮軍將軍 is Garrison General; army-pacifying invents a different title sense, and the proposed idiomatic restores the standard office name.

Winter, tenth month, day yiwei: Director of the Masters of Writing and newly appointed Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi was executed, as was Right Vice Director and newly appointed Army-Pacifying General Shen Wenji.

Winter, tenth month, day yiwei: Director of the Masters of Writing and newly appointed Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi was executed, as was Right Vice Director and newly appointed Garrison General Shen Wenji.
The literal of s0044 makes the same error on 鎮軍將軍; Garrison General is the correct office label.
Day dinghai: Prince Bao You of Shaoling, general who pacifies the barbarians, took Jiang.
Day dinghai: Prince Bao You of Shaoling, general who pacifies the barbarians, took Jiangzhou.
s0052 has 江州刺史; idiomatic Jiang truncates the province name, and Jiangzhou restores 江州.
Day yihai: Xiao Yi, newly relieved as right vice director of the masters of writing, became director.
Day yihai: Xiao Yi, newly appointed right vice director of the masters of writing, became director.
新除 means newly appointed to office, not newly relieved; the idiomatic of s0072 reverses that sense, and newly appointed corrects it.
Day yihai: the newly relieved Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xiao Yi was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
Day yihai: the newly appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xiao Yi was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
The literal repeats the same mistranslation of 新除 as newly relieved; newly appointed matches the Chinese.

Year three, spring, first month, day bingchen and the new moon: conjunction fell in the yin watch, eight marks before night's top; when the observances ended, palace women held the New Year court at Review-the-Troops Hall—the empress in her seat, eunuchs directing the rites, the emperor in armor looking on.

Year three, spring, first month, day bingshen and the new moon: conjunction fell in the yin watch, eight marks before night's top; when the observances ended, palace women held the New Year court at Review-the-Troops Hall—the empress in her seat, eunuchs directing the rites, the emperor in armor looking on.
s0091 dates the new moon 丙申 (bingshen), not 丙辰 (bingchen); the proposed idiomatic corrects the sexagenary day.

Year three, spring, first month, new moon on day bingchen: at the moment of conjunction the yin watch was eight marks before the top of the night; when the rites were done, the palace women held the New Year assembly at Review-the-Troops Hall; the empress took her proper seat, eunuchs conducted the ceremonies, and the emperor in martial dress attended to observe.

Year three, spring, first month, new moon on day bingshen: at the moment of conjunction the yin watch was eight marks before the top of the night; when the rites were done, the palace women held the New Year assembly at Review-the-Troops Hall; the empress took her proper seat, eunuchs conducted the ceremonies, and the emperor in martial dress attended to observe.
The literal likewise misreads 丙申 as bingchen; bingshen restores the correct day name.

Day dingyou: Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an, valiant-cavalry grand general, became grand tutor; Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an, newly made pacifying-army general, became general of chariots and cavalry with privilege equal to the three excellencies and an open staff.

Day dingyou: Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an, valiant-cavalry grand general, became Minister over the Masses; Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an, newly made pacifying-army general, became general of chariots and cavalry with privilege equal to the three excellencies and an open staff.
s0092 has 為司徒; 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅), and the proposed idiomatic corrects that office.

Day dingyou: Valiant-Cavalry Grand General Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an was made Grand Tutor; the newly appointed Pacifying-Army General Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies and an open office.

Day dingyou: Valiant-Cavalry Grand General Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an was made Minister over the Masses; the newly appointed Pacifying-Army General Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies and an open office.
The literal of s0092 likewise turns 司徒 into Grand Tutor; Minister over the Masses is the accurate office name.
That day the loyal army reached the south; twenty thousand of Shen Zhou's men at Gushu deserted to them.
That day the loyal army reached South Province; twenty thousand of Shen Zhou's men at Gushu fled back.
南州 is the place-name South Province, so replacing “the south” is right; but 奔歸 means fled back, not deserted to the loyal army, so the proposed after still invents a defection.
He asked leave to attend court twice daily; an edict refused and fixed him at once every three days.
He had the crown prince ask to attend court twice a day; an edict refused and set attendance at once every three days.
令太子求 is causative: someone had the crown prince request twice-daily court attendance; the idiomatic drops 太子 and the causative, and the proposed wording restores both.
The Founding Emperor's Xingguang Tower was finished in green lacquer; people called it the "Green Tower."
Emperor Shizu's Xingguang Tower was finished in green lacquer; people called it the "Green Tower."
s0156’s 世祖 is the temple name Shizu, not Founding Emperor (高祖/太祖); Emperor Shizu corrects that misidentification.
On the Founding Emperor's Xingguang Tower green lacquer was applied; the age called it the "Green Tower."
On Emperor Shizu's Xingguang Tower green lacquer was applied; the age called it the "Green Tower."
The literal likewise calls 世祖 the Founding Emperor; Emperor Shizu matches the temple name in the Chinese.

Baosun cursed the commanders; Xi Hao, valiant-cavalry general, stormed the enemy line in fury and was killed—Hao was a crack fighter, and with him gone the army broke; men leaped from Zhuque Tower or hurled themselves into the Huai till the dead could not be numbered.

Baosun cursed the commanders; Xi Hao, Direct-Gate General, stormed the enemy line in fury and was killed—Hao was a crack fighter, and with him gone the army broke; men leaped from Zhuque Tower or hurled themselves into the Huai till the dead could not be numbered.
s0189 titles Xi Hao 直閤將軍; valiant-cavalry confuses that office with later 驍將, and Direct-Gate General restores the actual title.

Baosun reviled the generals fiercely; Valiant Cavalry General Xi Hao, in a rage, charged the line and died—Hao was a fierce fighter; once he fell, the host collapsed; soldiers threw themselves from the Zhuque Watchtower or rushed into the Huai—dead beyond count.

Baosun reviled the generals fiercely; Direct-Gate General Xi Hao, in a rage, charged the line and died—Hao was a fierce fighter; once he fell, the host collapsed; soldiers threw themselves from the Zhuque Watchtower or rushed into the Huai—dead beyond count.
The literal makes the same office error on 直閤將軍; Direct-Gate General is correct, while 驍將 is only the descriptive ‘fierce fighter’ that follows.

Empress Dowager Xuande proclaimed: "The throne passed in turn; our forebears were sages together. The High Ancestor laid the splendid foundation and took heaven's register; the Martial Ancestor carried Ming forward and ended Wu; the Luminous High Ancestor renewed the bright estate—each died young, the palace carriage halted at dusk.

Empress Dowager Xuande proclaimed: "The throne passed in turn; our forebears were sages together. The High Ancestor laid the splendid foundation and took heaven's register; the Martial Ancestor continued the bright mandate in martial succession; the Luminous High Ancestor renewed the bright estate—each died young, the palace carriage halted at dusk.
係明下武 is classical succession diction (continuing bright mandate / martial succession), not ending a polity named Wu; the proposed idiomatic removes that invented conquest.

The High Ancestor fixed on the true heir, set the eldest son of the proper line, backed him with able men and worthy kin, braced court and camp to spare the state—yet before a year was out the boy turned butcher.

Gaozong fixed on the true heir, set the eldest son of the proper line, backed him with able men and worthy kin, braced court and camp to spare the state—yet before a year was out the boy turned butcher.
s0221’s subject is 高宗, Emperor Ming’s temple name; High Ancestor collides with 太祖 already so rendered in s0217, and Gaozong restores the correct referent.
He also hurried the imperial workshops for three hundred fine blades from the craftsmen, to furnish screens and fittings once the siege ended.
He also hurried the imperial workshops for three hundred fine blades from the craftsmen, intending them for clearance work once the siege ended.
待圍解以擬屏除 uses 屏除 as clearing away after the siege, not ornamental screens and fittings; the proposed idiomatic restores that sense.
